title: I kinda feel like AI gen same assets everywhere.
author: Free-Version-2746
selftext:
specially Claude. even got very fine tuned by me, it still look a lot of game I saw today. Saw same thing happen to people game too.

At this point, people will sooner or later call recognize it as a sign of AI slot lol

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body: I spent the first few months on mine to an asset builder in Claude for mine so I can hand make the assets or at least most and design the style to avoid that but I’ve noticed that other peoples asset builders look significantly like mine. So there’s definitely truth to that, Claude makes similar things the same way over and over

comments.author: Bitwizarding
comments.body: I make sure to make and place everything manually. Claude does a lot of the back-end work, but I have crooked fences and things misaligned like you would find in the real world

comments.author: Creepy-Doughnut-5054
comments.body:
Of course, because most just "Gimme mah asset bro" prompt and it just spits the same crap as for everyone else.  
Now, however, if you have clear vision on what you might want and iterate on it, you will absolutely get high quality stuff. But sure, that actually requires some effort most are not willing to put.

replies.author: kUkara4
replies.body:
Unfortunately (or fortunately) even after iterating it's still very sticky to its default style. Oftentimes I have to really dig into details and do one detail at a time. So precisely and specifically that it's not that different from me doing it myself, except AI does the job. And even then I have to keep reminding to NOT deviate, because it really likes to add extra noise of its own, which surely looks generic as always.

Pure AI games do all look the same and it makes them boring very quickly.

comments.author: HaphazardlyOrganized
comments.body: Yeah Claude seems to re used the UI for everyone.

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body:
This is exactly what happened with images, AI generates very similar characters, so to get what you want for 2D img2img AI must be used, so that the user can use an real image to add uniqueness to the AI.

Even when making 3D models I start from an custom drawing, generate an character, generate all sides, then take it to Meshi or Tripo.

comments.author: Significant_Tell407
comments.body: I mean its not Claude's fault you are incapable of giving a detailed prompt with a well defined art style. I just finished generating 25,000 art assets for my game in a art style I created and researched.

replies.author: Free-Version-2746
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/ej3nyupvpwth1.png?width=750&format=png&auto=webp&s=53759e0895978e02749be16137fccb50ac768523

for sure for sure

replies.author: Significant_Tell407
replies.body: Okay so what prompt did you use?

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body: "make 25000 assets in my artstyle. the artstyle is: what you are best at. happy creating. oh and dont bother me and just answer everything with yes."

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body: When I hear "What prompt did you use" in regards to something as complex and multifaceted as game dev especially when discussing how a visual language was expressed and built upon, I immediately become skeptical that the person who said it knows what they're asking for.

replies.author: Significant_Tell407
replies.body: then unfortunately you are not prepared for the future

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body: Yeesh

replies.author: Significant_Tell407
replies.body: Yea I'm sure AI Will just disappear like war, religion, and violence! So smart you are!

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body:
You seem to be making a strawman out of me. I never once claimed I was against AI. I simply (strongly) implied that reducing visual design down to a prompt. Especially for 25k assets without mentioning pipeline, software, tools, references, visual bibles made your claim dubious. 

LLMs have a tendency to default to a certain style over longform tasks, whether it be via text or through visual creations. Without the software and pipelines to ground it, your workflow will default to that "look" over time. That's why I was skeptical.

replies.author: Significant_Tell407
replies.body: Great. So let me explain i have 12 years of experience as a software engineer, graphical artists, animator and musician via piano. I drew 50 different images in an art style i have been drawing since i was 12. Then i used a combination of Klein  + LoRA trained on a [runpod.io](http://runpod.io) because i dont have enoug VRAM to train locally. This gave me a file i could use locally to generate sprites but also still needed more machines as for the variety in my project it would take 20+ weeks to do with a cheap ChatGPT plan (im spending enough on Claude as is). So i rented 6 GPUs and ran in parallel 25,000 sprite generations using my art style and combined visual vocabulary for the game im creating. Hope that explains that AI is a tool people use and not just a performative hack for reddit warriors.

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body: So basically what you're saying was that the prompt wasn't the important part? Glad we cleared that up.

replies.author: Significant_Tell407
replies.body: Each image had both my drawing and a prompt to change the visual that i previously drew. It would be physically impossible to automate without the prompt. But once again you dont know what you are talking about so...

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body: Nono, I got it. The prompts (plural) just got the ball rolling. So the whole "What prompt?" statement was just a gaff on your part and you would never actually imply a whole visual style can be narrowed down to a simple text prompt and actually requires a bevy of tools and tweaks to pull off. Glad we sorted that out. 👍

replies.author: Significant_Tell407
replies.body: It requires a pencil and a camera. You are just lazy and lack imagination as well as creativity. Skill less hacks criticize art rather than partaking in the endeavor.

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body: To be fair, you don't really know anything about me. The one listing off their resume over a light poking is you so. You've already confirmed my statement that a simple prompt isn't enough so I think we're done here.

comments.author: DudeWithASweater
comments.body: You need to prompt it to create better and more unique designs. Just going with the first generic generation it pulls up is going to get you a very generic asset

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body: Yes..... Unless you can make actual concepts that are distinct, cohesive, and give it art direction. Then it does not look the same.

comments.author: Vivid-Snow-2089
comments.body:
people just leave it up to default LLM taste will get.. the same default look

that's how it works

if you don't bring your own creativity and spark to a thing it will just be the same average that anyone else with the model gets

that's why when using AI its so important to have your own vision and make the LLM bend to that, not the other way around, if you are just going with the flow then you are already failing your project

comments.author: GridIron-Grit
comments.body: UI for sure

comments.author: CelestialButterflies
comments.body: I was thinking this earlier. I have seen so many 2.5d pixel art games on this sub in the last few weeks, and they all look the same... Everyone comments saying how nice it looks. Yes, it looks nice, but it also looks just like a game posted earlier. I was going to bring receipts but I'm useless on my phone, so... just a general agreement with you will have to do lol

replies.author: Ichi_Wang
replies.body:
I remember seeing one earlier today and top comment was someone accusing him of straight ripping off another one cause he saw an exact one like that. A few comments followed which also stated they saw several posted this week alone that all look the same.

Whether or not he straight ripped someone elses HD2.5D pixel-art game I wouldn't be surprised if he didn't and just got the same look as the other guy cause of this problem with the homogonous AI look

comments.author: DoctaRoboto
comments.body:
I've been posting about this for a long time, and it seems AI devs don't care, but I will post it again. The biggest challenge AI game devs will face in the near future won't be Anti-AIs but the lack of original visual styles. 

Gamers will get tired of the same AI-generic anime styles and the cleft-chin-faced realistic actors, same with assets and other visual elements. Good concepts, good plots, and original aesthetics (because mechanics would be too easy to steal) will be the difference between a succesful AI game and a flop.

replies.author: Tiamitsu
replies.body: Ah, those realistic characters with cleft chins. That’s probably the thing that bugs me the most every time. It’s just so typical of AI, lol.

replies.author: Dignified_Cyclops
replies.body: Majority of gamers can't even tell when purchased assets are being used, I don't think this will be as big of a problem as game devs think.

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body: I think it will become a problem. There are thousands of asset packs a dev can mix and match from to make an aesthetic. There are like two model right now that make things using the same aesthetic sense. People aren't going to notice the same sofa model popping up between two games among dozens. They will notice when half of their games are either Claude or OpenAI

replies.author: FlightFit335
replies.body: No they won't.  Look at your mobile games.  All the same as people finger fuck their screens.  Same shit different app and people eat it up.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body: Well, yea. It's because AIs have their own "personality" with design and tend to generate with the same or similar themes.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: When one-shotting the AI is going to pull from the easiest available sources. And many of these one-shots reference the same repositories of public assets or don't give specific references for creating assets in blender or otherwise, so it ends up just defaulting to whatever the likeliest styles are. So yes, of course you will mostly see that trend.

comments.author: TheReviewerWildTake
comments.body:
Tweak and edit those assets, after you got a foundation.   
  
I dunno why AI is mentioned so often only as "all or none" situations. It is not that different from a situation with web CSS templates , like tailwind, bootstrap etc. Usually they ended up "samey", but you could put some efforts to tweak them and make them look more unique. Or you could learn CSS and just do unique design from scratch.  
Kind of similar with AI. You can either heavily edit its foundation, or use it to scale your own custom stuff.

replies.author: Free-Version-2746
replies.body:
you either let AI make all or none your assets to make it cohesion looking.

tweak is as tiresome as make from scratch

replies.author: Nislaav
replies.body: Highly disagree, obviously depends on the asset you're making but droping a paint bucket on a specific part of an asset or resizing, cloning, adding vertices etc is far easier than starting with a blank page and a cube. To each their own of course, but spending 20ish min to add tweaks can go a long way per asset generated

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body:
probably because there are only so many ways you can animate your characters and there are also certain ways agents work best. i tried a "glass panel" ui and it was done like instantly and worked. i tried handpainted ai and everything was a fight and nothing  was simple. so guess which ui most people will use.

same with grafics

same with animations

same with sound

samer with everything. in pre-ai indy there were like 100 artstyles viable for solo devs. now there are like 5 viable for ai if you dont want to go 5x+ longer ~

comments.author: Dankenweenie
comments.body:
Simple fix, direct the art.

An easy example is referencing existing styles and it doesnt have to be a specific game per se.

Broad examples are: ps1 style, hand-drawn by a six year old, cel-shaded anime style, etc.

Start keeping a "mood board" of art styles that inspire you and literally feed those into the AI when prompting games and there's no way it should look the same.

Remember, the best artists steal but they dont copy!

comments.body: same ive seen the same golden ring in 5 others games and my own

comments.author: Tiamitsu
comments.body: If you take the time to develop the artistic side as well, it can really result in something very personal. If you struggle with that perhaps because you aren't very skilled at the artistic and visual aspect I would recommend focusing on gameplay development instead.

replies.author: zero0n3
replies.body: And then hire someone to do the art side down the road!

replies.author: One_Salty_Pigeon
replies.body: This is 100% my plan. Once I know this is a good avenue for me to make money etc. I will 100% be hiring people for all sorts of different work but especially anything related to art as well I suck at art. lol

comments.author: Maniick
comments.body: gimmie a picture so i can tell my agents not to make it look like that

comments.author: One_Salty_Pigeon
comments.body:
I really think it varies on the game as to how much that even matters. I love and love to create 'simulation' type games ex. shop sims etc. Now... my sims are more based around running a business, repetitive but addictive tasks like stocking shelves etc. I've noticed even though I'm putting in some effort to making my game look cool and have a real art style ALOT of those games don't and people tend to at least ignore it. Ex. most super market sims always have the 90s pixelated everything but the people are hyper realistic. I hate it but a-lot of people just don't care.

That being said what I have found is giving it direction or having something it can base it's design choices off is the easiest way to get solid 'unique' looking designs that don't just look like they were made by AI. Because you're basing it off real human work. Now with that being said if you just say make me a polygon blah blah than I'm sure it's going to look like everyone's polygon blah blah...

comments.author: FazedEclipse2
comments.body: I would actually say Claude has the better ceiling for uniqueness over chatgpt that defaults to a very standard very boring ai "standard" at least claude offers you diablo style UIs etc
